clue.text: Dramatist taking care of orphan maybe after Christmas

indicators.note: the care-and-orphan pieces are placed after the Christmas word in the build

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas
c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of
an orphan may be a ward, a child in someone's legal care

explanation.surface: A playwright looks after a parentless child once the Christmas holiday is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'care of' is written c/o on envelopes; 'taking' is a link word, and 'after' orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël Coward was an English playwright, famous for comedies such as Private Lives.

clue.text: Organ making din — one needs to escape

indicators.note: the numeral letter has to get out of the word for din, so it is removed

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A loud instrument is producing such a racket that one listener has to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs to escape' removes I from NOISE.
explanation.definitionFit: The smelling part of the face is a body organ.

clue.text: Graceful flying angel entering from beyond our world

indicators.note: the shuffled word goes inside the alien's two letters

parts.note: ET, the extraterrestrial, comes from beyond our world

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters of angel are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A graceful angel swoops down to Earth from outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' signals the anagram of ANGEL (giving LEGAN), and 'entering' the container; ET is the film's alien.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant describes someone or something with grace and refined style.

clue.text: Woman's hesitation over something wicked in seasonal act of worship

indicators.note: in a down clue the hesitation sits over, above, the wickedness piece

parts.note: Carol is a woman's name; with the possessive it gives CAROLS
er is the sound of someone hesitating
a vice is a wicked habit or sin

explanation.surface: A woman hesitates over some sin during a church service at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' means ER is placed above VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol service is a Christmas church service of hymns and readings, a seasonal form of worship.

clue.text: Victory spanning the world to become less plausible?

indicators.note: the victory word stretches round the planet word, holding it inside

parts.note: a victory is a win
the world we live on is the Earth

explanation.surface: A global triumph leaves the excuse looking flimsier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link, and the query marks the idiom: a story that wears thin, like worn cloth, convinces less.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: an excuse that wears thin grows less convincing, as cloth thins with use.

clue.text: Old magistrates, very English, laid into Welshman?

indicators.note: the two short letters are put inside the name, as if laid into it

parts.note: Rees is a typical Welsh name, so it stands for a Welshman, with the query signalling an example

explanation.surface: Ancient justices, very English, set about attacking a Welshman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid into' puts V and E inside REES; 'laid into' falsely suggests an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official or magistrate in medieval England.

clue.text: Unwanted message quietly received by pianist in film

indicators.note: the letter for quietly is taken in by the pianist's name

parts.note: Sam is the pianist in the film Casablanca, told to play it again
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A movie pianist is handed a note nobody wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received by' puts P inside SAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is junk email, unsolicited messages sent in bulk.

clue.text: It's gratefully received here and now — dispatched in advance?

definitions.meaning: a gift is received with thanks
the current time, as in 'at the moment'

explanation.walkthrough: Three senses of one word: a gift, the time now, and a jokey split into PRE and SENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A present is a gift, the present is now, and pre-sent means sent ahead.

clue.text: Remote inns dished out soup

indicators.note: food dished out is served around, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Isolated pubs served up some soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dished out' rearranges REMOTE INNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable soup.

clue.text: As we rather suspect, it's a bird

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or not right, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher says he rather suspects the creature is of a certain species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges AS WE RATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: The shearwater is a seabird that skims low over the waves.

clue.text: Restriction — Father Christmas's helpers reduced by half

indicators.note: only the first half of the helpers' name is kept

parts.note: Santa's sleigh is pulled by reindeer

explanation.surface: Santa's helpers are put on a strict regime and cut by half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by half' keeps REIN from REINDEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rein is a check or curb, as in keeping a rein on spending.

clue.text: Activity in which only some of the children are little angels

definitions.text: Activity in which only some of the children are little angels

parts.words: Activity in which only some of the children are little angels
parts.note: in a school Christmas show some pupils are cast as angels, while others play shepherds or kings

explanation.surface: Only some of the children are well behaved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little angels' seems to mean good children; it means pupils costumed as angels.
explanation.definitionFit: A school nativity play casts children as angels, shepherds and the holy family.

clue.text: Christmas cards? Mum has one left

parts.note: Ma is a word for mum
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Mum has one Christmas card left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas cards are an example of post, things delivered by the postman.

clue.text: Those growing up eat greens with difficulty

indicators.note: the letters are got through awkwardly, and so come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Youngsters struggle to finish their vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with difficulty' rearranges EAT GREENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescents aged thirteen to nineteen are young people still growing up.

clue.text: Evangelist is on Jerusalem's hill protected by mother at Christmas

indicators.note: the inner pieces are enclosed and shielded by the mother's name

parts.note: Mary is the mother of Jesus in the Christmas story
Sion, or Zion, is the hill of Jerusalem

explanation.surface: A preacher is on the holy hill of Jerusalem, sheltered by Mary at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: Sion is an older spelling of Zion; 'on' is a link word and 'protected by' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A missionary goes out to spread the Christian gospel, just as an evangelist does.

clue.text: Santa is often here going about

definitions.meaning: Santa flies by sleigh through the sky

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: up in the sky, and, of a rumour or feeling, spreading around.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means aloft, and also current or circulating, as excitement is.

clue.text: Season of snow — interminable?

indicators.note: of signals the answer is drawn out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Snow that seems to go on for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminable' pretends to describe the season; it is just where the letters sit, across snoW INTERminable.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter is the coldest of the four seasons of the year.

clue.text: A joint response that lacks proper thought?

definitions.text: A joint response that lacks proper thought?

parts.words: A joint response that lacks proper thought?
parts.note: a reflex from a leg joint when tapped, also an unthinking reaction

explanation.surface: A response made together that was not thought through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests shared, but it is the body joint whose reflex is tested with a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflexive, automatic reaction made without thinking, named after the knee reflex.

clue.text: Good person facing danger — ultimately I have to try very hard

parts.note: St, saint, is a good person

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of danger

parts.note: I've is the short form of I have

explanation.surface: A virtuous person in peril has to make a big effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive is to make great efforts towards a goal.

clue.text: Earfuls blasted to convey negative message

indicators.note: blasted means blown apart, so these letters are scattered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Being shouted at is a way of being told no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blasted' rearranges EARFULS.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a no, a message that turns something down.

clue.text: Ship takes fellow beyond part of the Commonwealth

indicators.note: the fellow is placed past, after, the country in the build

parts.note: India is a member of the Commonwealth
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A ship carries a man past a Commonwealth country.
explanation.walkthrough: An Indiaman was an East India Company trading ship; 'takes' is a link word and 'beyond' orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indiaman was a large merchant ship trading with India.

clue.text: Short note sent round hospital department as a reminder

indicators.note: the note is put round the department letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a memo is a short note
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A brief memo goes round a hospital ward to jog people's memory.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT (ear, nose and throat) is a standard hospital department; 'sent round' signals the container and 'as a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a souvenir, something kept to remind you of a person or event.

clue.text: Unrefined stuff in musical I composed

indicators.note: in shows the answer is held inside the run of these clue words

explanation.surface: Rough material appears in a musical written by the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to CALICO within musICAL I COmposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is plain cotton cloth, often unbleached, so a rough or unrefined fabric.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory — one church in which one has a limited time to perform ritual?

parts.note: food that is off is unsatisfactory
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the second group of pieces goes within the first numeral and church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
one is the Roman numeral I
time shortened to its abbreviation T

explanation.surface: A poor church where each priest has only a short slot to conduct the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' puts IAT inside ICE; 'has' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To officiate is to conduct a religious service or ceremony.

clue.text: Vegetables returning the end of this month

indicators.note: the month comes back, read backwards

parts.note: May is a month

indicators.note: the end of points to the final letter of this

explanation.surface: Vegetables come back into season at the close of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns MAY to YAM, and 'the end of' adds S from 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yams are starchy tuberous root vegetables.

clue.text: Wise Men had to — to observe King

parts.note: to observe is to see
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: The Magi had to see a King.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wise Men had to seek out the infant king; 'to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi had to search for the newborn Jesus, following the star.

clue.text: A model hiding nothing? Such may be seen in church!

definitions.text: Such may be seen in church

indicators.note: the zero letter is hidden away, so it goes missing from the pose word

parts.note: a model may pose for an artist
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A model wearing nothing would be a shock in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' removes O from POSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: I can sledge around, look, at an angle!

indicators.note: around signals the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of sledging round a slope at an angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges I CAN SLEDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideways glance is a look given out of the corner of the eye.

clue.text: It's said you will this festive tide

indicators.note: it's said marks that the spoken form of the next words is wanted

parts.note: contracted, you will is you'll

explanation.surface: Someone tells you that you'll be at this season.
explanation.walkthrough: YOU'LL said out loud matches the season word.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuletide is the old name for the Christmas season.

clue.text: Plodding that took couple to Bethlehem

definitions.meaning: Mary rode a donkey to Bethlehem with Joseph

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: grinding hard work, and literally the donkey's labour carrying Mary and Joseph.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard, dull toil, here also the donkey's literal labour.
